record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.original_question: Additional abelian U(1) gauge factors arise naturally in many MSSM extensions, but visible-sector U(1)′ breaking is constrained by supersymmetric scalar potentials and hidden-sector U(1) factors can communicate large D-term supersymmetry breaking through gauge kinetic mixing. How can extra U(1) gauge symmetries be incorporated into supersymmetric models without predicting unobserved weak-scale interactions or destabilizing the MSSM gauge hierarchy?

evidence.quote: Question #9 How do extra U(1)’s fit into SUSY?
The second possibility, by contrast, is in many ways more natural, but begs the question: if the new interactions should lie near the weak scale, where are they?
Since for a U(1) interaction the gauge field strength tensor Fµν is gauge-invariant, the Lagrangian can contain terms which mix the field strengths of two different U(1)’s.
Such contributions, if present, destabilize the gauge hierarchy in the MSSM.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider supersymmetric extensions of the Standard Model (the MSSM) augmented by one or more additional abelian gauge factors U(1)′. Such extra U(1)′ symmetries may live in the visible sector, in which case their spontaneous breaking is governed by a supersymmetric scalar potential involving MSSM-charged or singlet fields, or they may live in a hidden sector that is coupled to the visible sector only gravitationally and through the gauge-invariant kinetic mixing operator

  L_mix = -(ε/2) F^Y_{μν} F'^{μν},

where F^Y is the hypercharge field strength and F' is the field strength of the hidden U(1)′. In a supersymmetric context this mixing extends to the superfield level and, when the hidden U(1)′ has a nonzero D-term from supersymmetry breaking, induces visible-sector soft mass-squared contributions of order ε times the hidden D-term, which generically destabilize the electroweak hierarchy.

Problem. Construct (or prove obstructions to constructing) a consistent supersymmetric model containing one or more additional U(1) gauge factors, beyond the MSSM gauge group SU(3)_c × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y, satisfying all of the following:
1. Anomaly cancellation, including mixed anomalies with the MSSM gauge factors, is achieved with a phenomenologically acceptable matter content.
2. The extra U(1) symmetry is spontaneously broken, with the associated Z′ boson (and any accompanying matter or interactions) either sufficiently heavy or sufficiently weakly coupled to evade all current experimental bounds on weak-scale gauge interactions.
3. Any gauge kinetic mixing ε between the extra U(1) factors and U(1)_Y, together with the associated D-term contributions to visible-sector scalar masses, does not destabilize the MSSM gauge hierarchy, i.e. soft masses for MSSM scalars remain near the electroweak scale.
4. The model is compatible with standard mechanisms of supersymmetry breaking and mediation.

Either exhibit such a model explicitly, or prove a no-go statement delimiting which combinations of U(1) charge assignments, breaking scales, and kinetic-mixing parameters are admissible.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how extra U(1) gauge factors can be consistently embedded in supersymmetric models without unobserved weak-scale phenomena or destabilization of the MSSM hierarchy remains an active area of research. Foundational work on kinetic mixing and the SUSY gauge hierarchy (Dienes–Kolda–March-Russell, 1996) established the destabilization problem, and subsequent work through 2025 (string-theoretic kinetic mixing, dark gauge mediation, singlet portals) continues to propose partial solutions in specific frameworks (e.g. low-scale gauge mediation, particular string compactifications), but no general resolution has been established.

status_evidence.title: Kinetic Mixing and the Supersymmetric Gauge Hierarchy
status_evidence.snippet: Kinetic mixing between hypercharge and hidden U(1) factors generates SUSY-breaking contributions that can destabilize the MSSM hierarchy.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the destabilization problem from kinetic mixing in SUSY hidden sectors.

status_evidence.title: Kinetic Mixing of the Photon with Hidden U(1)s in String Phenomenology
status_evidence.snippet: Exchange of heavy messengers leads to kinetic mixing between hypercharge and hidden-sector U(1)s, testable in upcoming experiments.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research into the size and phenomenology of kinetic mixing with hidden U(1)s.

status_evidence.title: Dark gauge-mediated supersymmetry breaking with a massless dark photon
status_evidence.snippet: Large kinetic mixing induces significant distortions to superpartner spectra in dark gauge-mediated SUSY breaking.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work shows the problem of extra U(1)s and SUSY mediation remains actively studied without a settled general answer.
